# Terrarium

> A societal simulation engine where LLM-powered agents form emergent civilizations.

Terrarium is a societal petri dish: you make a world with rules, fill it with AI agents, one mind per person, and see what grows. Each agent has a personality, needs, memories and beliefs that can be wrong. Nothing like markets, chiefs or alliances is written into the code; the question is whether such structure emerges on its own. It is for anyone curious about agent-based models, emergence and artificial societies. The engine is written in Rust. A viewer compiled to WebAssembly runs in the browser at https://terrarium.raskell.io/play/ , entirely on the visitor's machine with nothing sent anywhere; there, people act on instinct, rules taken from behavioural ecology and social psychology. Built from source, it runs in a terminal, and with an Anthropic API key every person deliberates through Claude. Terrarium is free and open source under the MIT license, and is in active development.

## Links

- [Terrarium](https://terrarium.raskell.io/): the website
- [Watch a world](https://terrarium.raskell.io/play/): the browser viewer

- [raskell.io apps](https://raskell.io/apps/): Terrarium among the other apps by the author
- [Author](https://raskell.io/about/): Raffael Schneider
